CHAPTER 35 · VERGLEICHSARBEIT · DRESS REHEARSAL · BGY YEAR 11

Dress rehearsal part B

Three tasks, 30 marks, about 65 minutes: that is part B of the Vergleichsarbeit. Have the MMS and formula booklet ready, start the clock and only look at the solutions at the end.

PART B30 MARKS65 MINUTES
WHAT IS TESTED
  • All three tasks in one go
  • Marks for every part, as in the real paper
  • A long real-life task set in Saxony: system of equations, parabola, trigonometry

$90$ minutes in total, part A takes $25$ minutes. How many minutes are left for part B?

$90 - 25 = 65$

How many marks does this part B have?

$8 + 7 + 15 = 30$

From how many of the $45$ marks do you get a 4 in the Vergleichsarbeit?

According to the scale of the last two years, $18$ to $24$ marks give a 4.

TOOLKITWHAT YOU NEED FOR THIS CHAPTER

TASK 1LEVEL I · REPRODUCING

1Parabola and line

Task B1 · Function (8 marks). All three tasks are to be done. Part B begins as soon as part A has been collected after 25 minutes; 90 minutes are available for both parts together. The MMS, the formula booklet and drawing instruments are allowed. — The function $f$ defined on $\mathbb{R}$ is given by $f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x + 6$.

State the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of $f$ and calculate the zeros of $f$. (3 marks)

Completing the square: $f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^2 - 4x) + 6 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 2)^2 + 8$; the vertex is $S(2, 8)$. Zeros: after multiplying by $-2$, $-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x + 6 = 0$ becomes $x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0$, so $x = 2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 12} = 2 \pm 4$. The zeros are $x_1 = -2$ and $x_2 = 6$.

The line $g$ passes through the point $P$ where the graph of $f$ crosses the $y$-axis and through the point $Q$ where it crosses the positive $x$-axis. Find an equation of $g$ and prove that $g$ and the graph of $f$ have no common points apart from $P$ and $Q$. (2 marks)

$P(0, 6)$ and $Q(6, 0)$ give the gradient $m = \frac{0 - 6}{6 - 0} = -1$ and hence $g(x) = -x + 6$. Set equal: $-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x + 6 = -x + 6$, so $-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 3x = 0$ and $x \cdot \left(3 - \frac{1}{2}x\right) = 0$. The only solutions $x = 0$ and $x = 6$ belong to $P$ and $Q$.

A line $h$ parallel to $g$ has exactly one point $B$ in common with the graph of $f$. Find an equation of $h$ and the coordinates of $B$. (3 marks)

Approach $h(x) = -x + n$. Set equal and multiply by $-2$: $x^2 - 6x + 2n - 12 = 0$. There is exactly one solution if the discriminant is zero: $9 - (2n - 12) = 0$, so $n = 10.5$. Then $x = 3$ is the only solution, with $f(3) = -4.5 + 6 + 6 = 7.5$. Result: $h(x) = -x + 10.5$ and $B(3, 7.5)$. A second way: for a parabola, the point of contact of a line parallel to the chord $\overline{PQ}$ lies exactly above the midpoint of $0$ and $6$, i.e. at $x = 3$; from $7.5 = -3 + n$ again $n = 10.5$.

TASK 2LEVEL II · MAKING CONNECTIONS

2The Christmas pyramid

Task B2 · Solids and chance (7 marks). A workshop in the Ore Mountains makes Christmas pyramids. It casts the candles for them itself: each candle consists of a cylinder $1.4$ cm across and $9$ cm high with a conical tip $1$ cm high on top (see figure).

The wax is delivered in cuboid blocks measuring $25\ \mathrm{cm} \times 12\ \mathrm{cm} \times 8\ \mathrm{cm}$. In casting, $5\%$ of the wax is lost. Find the maximum number of candles that can be cast from one block. (3 marks)

Volume of a candle: $V = \pi \cdot 0.7^2 \cdot 9 + \frac{1}{3} \cdot \pi \cdot 0.7^2 \cdot 1 \approx 13.85 + 0.51 \approx 14.37\ \mathrm{cm}^3$. A block of wax has $25 \cdot 12 \cdot 8 = 2400\ \mathrm{cm}^3$, of which $95\%$ can be used, i.e. $2280\ \mathrm{cm}^3$. Since $\frac{2280}{14.37} \approx 158.7$, at most 158 candles can be cast.

A box holds $10$ carved figures for the pyramid, $6$ angels and $4$ miners. For the top tier two figures are taken out at random one after the other without replacement. Calculate the probability that two angels are taken, and the probability that there is at least one miner among them. (2 marks)

Two angels: $P = \frac{6}{10} \cdot \frac{5}{9} = \frac{30}{90} = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.333$. “At least one miner” is its complementary event: $P = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.667$.

A child claims: “Two figures of the same kind are more likely than two different ones.” Assess this statement. (2 marks)

Two of the same kind: $\frac{30}{90} + \frac{4}{10} \cdot \frac{3}{9} = \frac{30}{90} + \frac{12}{90} = \frac{7}{15} \approx 0.467$. Two different ones: $2 \cdot \frac{6}{10} \cdot \frac{4}{9} = \frac{48}{90} = \frac{8}{15} \approx 0.533$. The statement is false; two different figures are somewhat more likely.

TASK 3LEVEL III · EVALUATING

3A day in Moritzburg

Task B3 (15 marks). A school class visits Moritzburg Castle, which stands on an island in the castle pond.

Three groups pay for a guided tour of the castle: $2$ adults, $1$ concession and $2$ children together €$43$, $1$ adult and $3$ concessions together €$39$, and $4$ adults and $5$ children together €$73$. Use a system of linear equations to find the three admission prices. (3 marks)

With $e$, $r$ and $k$ for the prices in euros: $2e + r + 2k = 43$, $e + 3r = 39$ and $4e + 5k = 73$, in matrix form $\begin{pmatrix}2 & 1 & 2\\1 & 3 & 0\\4 & 0 & 5\end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix}e\\r\\k\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}43\\39\\73\end{pmatrix}$. The MMS gives $e = 12$, $r = 9$ and $k = 5$: adults pay €$12$, concessions €$9$ and children €$5$. Check with the first group: $24 + 9 + 10 = 43$.

A footbridge at the castle pond has a parabolic arch (figure 1). In a coordinate system with the water surface as the $x$-axis (one unit corresponds to $1$ m), the arch begins at $P_1(0, 0)$, ends at $P_2(8, 0)$ and passes through $P_3(2, 1.5)$. Use a system of linear equations to find an equation of the parabola and state the greatest height of the arch above the water. (4 marks)

Approach $p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$. From $P_1$ it follows that $c = 0$; from $P_2$ and $P_3$, $64a + 8b = 0$ and $4a + 2b = 1.5$. The first equation gives $b = -8a$; substituted, $4a - 16a = 1.5$, so $a = -0.125$ and $b = 1$. So $p(x) = -0.125x^2 + x$. By symmetry the vertex lies in the middle at $x = 4$: $p(4) = -2 + 4 = 2$. The arch is at most $2$ m high.

A pleasure boat with a sun roof is $3$ m wide and $1.6$ m high up to the top edge of the roof. Check whether it can pass under the arch in the middle, and find the maximum width of a boat that is $1.6$ m high. (4 marks)

In the middle means: the boat reaches from $x = 2.5$ to $x = 5.5$. There $p(2.5) = p(5.5) \approx 1.72$ m, more than $1.6$ m: the boat fits through with just under $12$ cm to spare. Greatest width: after multiplying by $-8$, $p(x) = 1.6$ gives the equation $x^2 - 8x + 12.8 = 0$ with $x = 4 \pm \sqrt{3.2}$, so $x_1 \approx 2.21$ and $x_2 \approx 5.79$. A boat $1.6$ m high may be at most $2\sqrt{3.2} \approx 3.58$ m wide.

A rowing boat travels in a straight line $260$ m from the boat hire $B$ to a buoy $T$, changes its direction there by $48°$ and travels another $190$ m in a straight line to the landing stage $A$ at the castle (figure 2). Calculate the length of the direct route from $B$ to $A$ and the size of the angle $\angle TBA$. (4 marks)

In the triangle $BTA$ the angle at $T$ is not $48°$ but its supplementary angle $180° - 48° = 132°$. Cosine rule: $\overline{BA}^2 = 260^2 + 190^2 - 2 \cdot 260 \cdot 190 \cdot \cos 132° \approx 169\,810$, so $\overline{BA} \approx 412$ m. Sine rule: $\sin\angle TBA = \frac{190 \cdot \sin 132°}{412.1} \approx 0.343$, so $\angle TBA \approx 20.0°$. The angle is certainly acute, because it lies opposite the shortest side.

LOOKING BACKTHE IDEA AND THE TRAP

TASK 1 · PARABOLA AND LINE

Vertex and zeros, then the line through the intercepts. For touching, the discriminant must be zero.

Trap: when multiplying by $-2$, all terms change sign, including the constant: $6 - n$ becomes $2n - 12$. In c), $B$ is not a point of intersection as in b) but a point of contact: the discriminant must be zero, not positive.

TASK 2 · THE CHRISTMAS PYRAMID

Cylinder plus cone, $5\%$ loss, then round down. Without replacement the second fraction changes.

Trap: without replacement the second fraction changes: after an angel there are only $9$ figures left in the box, $5$ of them angels. With replacement you would get $0.6 \cdot 0.6 = 0.36$ for two angels, and the statement in c) would even be true, with $0.36 + 0.16 = 0.52$ for two of the same kind.

TASK 3 · A DAY IN MORITZBURG

System of equations, parabola, width for passing through and a cosine rule with $180° - 48°$: across everything, as in every Vergleichsarbeit.

Trap: in d), $48°$ is the change of direction, not the angle in the triangle. If you calculate with $48°$, you get $\overline{BA} \approx 194$ m, less than the first leg, although the boat moves further away from $B$ after the buoy. — Marking: part B has 30 marks; with part A (15 marks) it is 45 marks. Grading scale: from 39 marks grade 1, 32 to 38 marks grade 2, 25 to 31 marks grade 3, 18 to 24 marks grade 4, 9 to 17 marks grade 5, up to 8 marks grade 6. Up to 2 marks can be deducted for poor presentation.

TESTTHE SAME IDEAS, NEW NUMBERS
ROUND 1

What is the larger zero of $-\frac{1}{2}x^2 + 2x + 6$?

$x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0$, so $(x - 6)(x + 2) = 0$.

$6$ angels and $4$ miners, two drawn without replacement. What is the probability of two miners?

$\frac{4}{10} \cdot \frac{3}{9} = \frac{12}{90} = \frac{2}{15}$

ROUND 2

A boat changes its direction by $48°$. What is the angle in the triangle at this corner, in degrees?

$180° - 48° = 132°$

A cylinder has $r = 1$ cm and $h = 9$ cm. Its volume is $k \cdot \pi$ cm³. What is $k$?

$\pi \cdot 1^2 \cdot 9 = 9\pi$
